title: Hosted API feature intake: queue classifier and response-contract onboarding playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers and power users submit multi-purpose Hosted API requests that mix chat, streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. We lack a consistent intake classifier and a lightweight contract-onboarding flow that (a) determines routing priority and SLA band, (b) captures required security/compliance signals, and (c) generates an explicit response contract (expected output shape, latency SLO, fallback model) engineers can depend on. This ticket defines a playbook to build a queue-classifier + response-contract onboarding UX and triage rules for Hosted API feature requests (non-bug).
background: Current intake is largely manual—PMs and solutions engineers read customer notes, infer priority and required features, then open follow-ups. That process is slow, inconsistent, and leaks signals (e.g., streaming required, tool chains present, structured output schema). Several enterprise customers reported onboarding delays when their app needs streaming with synchronous tool calls and schema-validated outputs. We also see increased operational incidents when we misclassify expected consistency/latency requirements.
scope: Design and implement: (1) a lightweight classifier that tags inbound Hosted API feature requests with attributes: communication type (chat vs. prompt), delivery mode (streaming vs non-streaming), tool/function-calling present, structured-output schema required, SLA sensitivity, data residency constraints; (2) a response-contract template that captures required model variant, max acceptable latency, deterministic flags, and fallback policy; (3) a gated onboarding checklist for enterprise customers that ensures security/compliance signals are recorded before routing to Dedicated/Private sales motion; (4) integration with Linear intake form, Confluence template, and Console intake dashboard for visibility.
out_of_scope: Implementing runtime enforcement of contracts (handled by runtime team), building model routing automation beyond tagging, on-prem installation guides.
success_metrics:
- Median time from intake creation to assignment drops from 4 days to 8 hours for enterprise feature requests.
- >85% of intake items contain a completed response-contract template.
- Fewer misrouted requests: reduction in reassignments by 60%.
- Positive pilot feedback from 3 enterprise customers on onboarding clarity.
acceptance_criteria:
- Intake form updated with classifier fields and required signals.
- Response-contract Confluence template created and linked in the intake form.
- Dashboard shows classifier tags and SLA bands for >90% of new requests.
- Pilot with Solutions & Sales runs for 4 customers and produces documented adjustments.
- Product + Legal sign-off on minimum compliance fields.
rollout_plan: 1) Draft intake form and response contract template (this ticket). 2) Run 4-week pilot with Solutions for new enterprise requests. 3) Iterate on template based on pilot feedback. 4) Launch company-wide intake update and notify sales/PS/SE teams. 5) Add automated reminders and gating for missing compliance signals.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Overly heavy intake slows conversion. Mitigation: Keep contract template minimal; mark extra fields optional.
- Risk: Sales/SEs ignore new fields. Mitigation: Training sessions + small incentive (reduced triage SLA) during pilot.
- Risk: Misalignment with runtime capabilities. Mitigation: Early sync with Runtime and Dedicated teams; include runtime owner as stakeholder.
deliverables: Pilot run notes and final checklist
updates: 2026-03-02: Draft intake fields proposed; reached out to Runtime for schema mapping.
2026-03-05: Design provided mockups for compact response-contract; suggested collapsing latency + determinism into single SLA band selector.
2026-03-08: Solutions team volunteered 4 enterprise onboarding candidates for pilot.
2026-03-10: Legal requested KMS/key-management checkbox; added to required compliance signals.
2026-03-12: PM review with Engineering; agreed to build the classifier as a thin rule-based first pass (no ML) and revisit after pilot.
next_steps: 1) Finalize intake form fields and publish Confluence template by 2026-03-16. 2) Coordinate pilot kickoff with Solutions (target 2026-03-22). 3) Hand off minimal implementation ticket to Eng: ENG- for intake form + dashboard integration.
notes_for_engineering: Classifier should be rule-driven and extensible; expose tags as comma-separated strings in Linear so Console dashboard can filter. Response-contract must include an optional JSON schema URL field for structured outputs. Provide simple webhook to notify Solutions when SLA band is High.
final_decision: Playbook approved for pilot; classifier to be rules-first and templated response-contract will be mandatory for enterprise-tier intake.
review_feedback: Design: keep template under 6 fields to avoid friction
Legal: require KMS checkbox for Private/Dedicated paths
Runtime: confirmed fallback model field is necessary for safe routing
